critique:
the policy prompt for subgoal
  The failure occurred while executing a goal to pick up the container hiding the red cube and then the container hiding the blue cube. After the first pickup, put-down execution showed the fingers opening fully and remaining fully open as the hand retreated upward, but the final observation still described a container as lifted off the table. The memory correctly contained only the second target, remaining_targets=[[141, 78]]. The policy chose B instead of A on that remaining target. This breaks SUFFICIENCY: the policy prompt did not clearly resolve conflicting release evidence and lifted-container detection, allowing its held-container fallback to override a completed release. Strengthen the put-down transition rule: observed finger opening to full release followed by hand retreat with the fingers remaining fully open establishes that the hand is empty and the put-down is complete, even if an object detection still describes a container as lifted. When remaining_targets is nonempty, choose A on the container corresponding to its first point. Give this release rule priority over the held-container fallback. Restrict that fallback so a lifted-container report alone cannot establish holding in the presence of an observed release; retain grasp-and-lift evidence with maintained partial closure as evidence of holding when no subsequent release is observed. No other subgoal rules need removal or replacement.
